candidateEvidence.excerpt: Jacob Coxon said in a post that he had resigned from Anthropic after three years working on AI pretraining at Anthropic and OpenAI

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Primary statement and independent confirmations; no universal local date is assigned to the post.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.
WIRED reports that Coxon worked on pretraining at Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI.
Coxon told WIRED that possible threats could include AI-enabled biological threats or cyberweapons; WIRED did not establish either feared outcome as having occurred.
Coxon recommends that OpenAI and Anthropic coordinate on limiting recursive self-improvement—the use of AI to build new AI systems—and ultimately seeks international coordination.
Coxon said Anthropic operates more responsibly than OpenAI in his experience, but predicted that competition could force future trade-offs between rigor and safety.
Asked whether Anthropic was already cutting corners, Coxon answered: No, not yet. It's not cutting any corners.
Anthropic told WIRED that the industry would benefit from a lawful, verifiable way to work together to pace releases of powerful models.
OpenAI did not return WIRED's request for comment.
ABC reported Coxon's September 9 resignation statement and his work at Anthropic and OpenAI.
ABC separately reported Hubinger's personal greater-than-ten-percent estimate and his statement that Anthropic was trying its best.
